audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..3].side read "Skill" against win[0..3] "Orianna", and phases[6].side reads "Skill" against win[6] "Anivia" — five rows contradicting between layers.
audit.why: Command: Attack costs 35 mana on a 7s cooldown falling to 3s and outranges nothing Anivia can answer pre-6; Anivia's 55.34% over 730 games comes from the storm and the late-game zone, which is exactly what row 7 describes.
Lost Chapter / level 6 / Seraph's-RoA is right, and Orianna's own spike is Command: Shockwave at 6 on 110s at rank 1, dropping to 80s at rank 3.
audit.corrected: Wrote the 110s number so the commit window is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: Command: Shockwave is described as her "sidestep tool", and nothing states the interaction that actually decides trades: Command: Protect (E, 9s) shields her and adds Armor and MR right through your Flash Frost into Frostbite burst. Shockwave's real geometry — 410 range, pulling enemies toward the ball after a delay — is never given.
audit.why: Anivia's whole damage pattern is one burst on a chilled target. A 9s shield eats it, and forcing E out first is the single highest-value sequencing rule in this lane.
audit.corrected: Named the shield, the 9s window, and Shockwave's pull-toward-the-ball geometry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet reports zero cooldown-sequencing cues in this matchup.
audit.why: Q at 7s falling to 3s, W at a flat 7s, E at 9s and R at 110s are all needed to know when stepping up is safe.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns and the phase whys.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Orianna

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Anivia

edits.before: A wave-clear war you eventually win — survive his range early, then R erases waves while your stun threatens his face.
edits.after: A wave-clear war you eventually win — survive her 35-mana ball poke, then R erases waves faster than she can re-place it.

edits.before: Survive the early range war, then out-clear and out-zone him with storm + wall. Track Command: Shockwave before every commit and keep the wave where your pattern works.
edits.after: Survive the early range war, then out-clear and out-zone her with storm and wall. Force Command: Protect out before you burst — a 9s shield eats the whole chilled Frostbite.

edits.before: Orianna wins by landing Command: Shockwave, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Orianna wins by shielding through your burst on a 9s cooldown, then pulling you off the egg into her team with Shockwave.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Orianna burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Bait Command: Protect with a Frostbite first, then in its 9 seconds land Flash Frost and Frostbite again — the doubled chill damage lands unshielded.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Orianna walks straight at you.
edits.after: Opening with Flash Frost into a ball she still holds — she shields, Dissonance slows you, and your 80-mana Q bought nothing at all.

edits.before: - Orianna Command: Shockwave: matchup-defining — The fight-flipping wombo — track the ball position like a second enemy. It governs your forward steps. - W Crystallize spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Command: Protect: 9s of shield plus Armor and MR — force it out before every burst. - Command: Attack: 35 mana, 7s down to 3s, so the poke never stops. - Shockwave: 110s at rank 1, 410 range, pulls you to the ball. - Crystallize is for that pull.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by making her ball choose: it either sits forward for poke or back on a shield, never both — punish whichever half of the lane it leaves open.

edits.before: If Orianna gets one kill, respect Command: Shockwave and reset to farming. Two kills: play for the team, not for solo redemption — farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.
edits.after: If Orianna gets one kill, never stand inside the 410 range her Shockwave needs. Two kills: farm with R wave-clear from max distance, hold Crystallize for the pull, and stop trying to out-poke a 35-mana Q.

edits.before: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Orianna away from the comeback farm, and rotate first to every river fight with your stun loaded.
edits.after: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Orianna off the comeback farm, and step up whenever Command: Protect is on its 9s — she is immobile without it.

edits.before: Q only — last-hit with autos and save the stun strictly for his step-ups. Your egg is NOT a license to int level 1.
edits.after: Q only — last-hit with autos and hold the stun; her Clockwork Windup stacks on you if you stand for autos. The egg is NOT a license to int level 1.

edits.before: Q-E online — a landed stun now means a real chunk. Trade only when his engage tool is down; your mana hates wasted rotations.
edits.after: Q-E online — a landed stun means a real chunk, but only after Command: Protect is spent; her 9s shield otherwise eats the whole rotation.

edits.before: Full basic kit: W cuts the lane in half. Wall his path to the wave when your jungler shadows — free stun setups.
edits.after: Full basic kit: Crystallize cuts the lane in half. Wall her retreat when your jungler shadows — she has no dash, only a 225-radius slow field.

edits.before: The fight-flipping wombo — track the ball position like a second enemy. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Track the ball like a second enemy — with it on an ally she can shield and Shockwave from 410 range away.

edits.before: That is Orianna’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Command: Protect refreshes every 9s — Q into a shielded target is 80 mana spent on nothing.

edits.before: Orianna's Command: Dissonance poke and ball-zoning let her control the wave and threaten a Shockwave setup before your kit has enough range or a wall to answer.
edits.after: Command: Attack costs her 35 mana on a 7s cooldown while your Q costs 80 — she can zone the wave and shield the answer before you have Glacial Storm.

edits.before: Anivia's zone control and burst combo out-scale Orianna's ball-dependent kit — walling her ball away neutralizes most of her kit outright.
edits.after: Anivia's zone control out-scales her: Shockwave is 410 range on 80s even maxed, so a stormed choke and a wall on the pull line ends her fight.

edits.before: She continues to out-poke and out-position you through the early game
edits.after: A 35-mana Q on 7s out-pokes your 80-mana one every time

edits.before: She keeps lane control right up to your level 6 spike
edits.after: Command: Protect still shields out your burst up to level 6

edits.before: Watch for her ball placement before committing to trades
edits.after: Force Command: Protect out before you commit a trade

edits.before: Set up a Shockwave pick with allies before your ultimate is up
edits.after: Shield through your burst, then Shockwave you into her team

notes: Orianna is female; tldr, winCon, phases[0-2].why, breakdown.wave and several report entries said "his/him" — corrected where edited. I deliberately removed the claim in spikes[3].text that Crystallize can separate Orianna from her ball: the kits do not establish whether the ball's return path is stopped by terrain, and the same claim also sits in content.late, which I left alone rather than assert either way.
